title: Wishes and Requests
grammarNote: The present subjunctive appears in the second clause after verbs of will, request, or emotion (querer que, pedir que, esperar que, alegrar que, ojalá que) when the subject changes — compare 'quiero ir' (same subject, infinitive) with 'quiero que vayas' (different subject, subjunctive). Regular endings: -ar verbs take -e/-es/-e/-emos/-en (hable, hables, hable, hablemos, hablen); -er/-ir verbs take -a/-as/-a/-amos/-an (coma, comas, coma, comamos, coman). Key irregulars to memorize: sea (ser), vaya (ir), tenga (tener), haga (hacer), pueda (poder).

phrases.target: Quiero que vengas a la fiesta
phrases.native: I want you to come to the party
phrases.phonetic: kee-EH-ro keh VEN-gas ah lah FYES-tah
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Querer que' triggers the subjunctive whenever the wisher and the doer are different people — here 'yo quiero' but 'tú vengas'.

exampleSentence.target: Quiero que vengas temprano a la fiesta.
exampleSentence.native: I want you to come early to the party.

phrases.grammarNote: Contrast: 'quiero venir' (I want to come, same subject, infinitive) vs. 'quiero que vengas' (I want you to come, different subject, subjunctive of venir).
phrases.memoryHook: Picture yourself pointing at a friend and saying 'quiero QUE tú vengas' — the 'que' is the pivot where the subject changes.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: I want you to come to the party
practiceItems.answer: Quiero que vengas a la fiesta

practiceItems.prompt: ¿Qué quieres que yo haga esta noche?
practiceItems.answer: Quiero que vengas a la fiesta

phrases.target: Te pido que traigas el pastel
phrases.native: I'm asking you to bring the cake
phrases.phonetic: teh PEE-doh keh TRY-gas el pas-TEL
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Pedir que' (to ask/request that) is one of the clearest request triggers for the subjunctive; 'traigas' is the irregular subjunctive of 'traer'.

exampleSentence.target: Te pido que traigas el pastel a las seis.
exampleSentence.native: I'm asking you to bring the cake at six.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Traer' has an irregular subjunctive stem 'traig-': traiga, traigas, traiga, traigamos, traigan.
phrases.memoryHook: Think 'traigas' sounds like 'try-gas' — 'try to bring the gas... I mean the cake'.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: I'm asking you to bring the cake
practiceItems.answer: Te pido que traigas el pastel

practiceItems.prompt: ¿Qué le pides a tu amigo que haga?
practiceItems.answer: Te pido que traigas el pastel

phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Esperar que' (to hope that) is an emotion trigger for the subjunctive; 'salga' is the irregular subjunctive of 'salir'.

exampleSentence.target: Espero que todo salga bien en la fiesta.
exampleSentence.native: I hope everything goes well at the party.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Salir' forms its subjunctive from the stem 'salg-': salga, salgas, salga, salgamos, salgan.
phrases.memoryHook: Link 'salga' to 'salga el sol' — 'may the sun come out' — a classic hopeful subjunctive.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: I hope everything goes well
¿Qué esperas para la fiesta de esta noche?

phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Ojalá' comes from Arabic 'law šā' allāh' (God willing) and always takes the subjunctive, with or without 'que'.

exampleSentence.target: Ojalá que ella pueda venir a la fiesta.
exampleSentence.native: I hope she can come to the party.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Poder' has the irregular subjunctive stem 'pued-' with a vowel shift: pueda, puedas, pueda, podamos, puedan.
phrases.memoryHook: 'Ojalá' sounds like 'oh, holla!' — an excited wish shouted out loud.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: I hope she can come
¿Qué esperas de tu amiga para la fiesta?

phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Alegrarse que' / 'me alegra que' expresses emotion and always requires the subjunctive in the second clause.

phrases.native: I want you to be happy
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Sea' is the irregular subjunctive of 'ser', one of the five essential irregulars for this lesson.

dialogue.scenario: The learner calls two friends to organize a surprise birthday party.
